questions: What happens when a player chooses an index i where A_i = 0 - is this considered an invalid move?
Does the game end immediately when S becomes empty, or does it end after all possible moves are exhausted?
When multiple indices have the same value, how is the tie broken for optimal play decisions?
Is there a specific order in which players must process indices, or can they choose any valid index?
What constitutes "the last operation" - the final move that causes S to become empty, or the move that makes it impossible to continue?
Are players allowed to make moves that don't change the set S (when choosing an index already in S)?
How exactly is the winning condition checked - after each move or only when no more moves are possible?
Does the constraint "it can be proven that until a winner is determined" guarantee that the game cannot end in a draw?
answers: A player may not choose an index with A_i = 0; only indices with A_i ≥ 1 are valid.
The game ends immediately once S becomes {1,2,...,N} (not empty), right after the operation that completes it.
Not applicable; a player may freely choose among valid indices, no tie-breaking is specified.
No specific order is required; a player may choose any index satisfying A_i ≥ 1.
'The last operation' is the operation that makes S = {1,2,...,N}; that operation's performer wins.
Yes, a player may choose an index already in S; this simply decrements A_i without changing S.
The winning condition (S becoming the full set) is checked immediately after each operation.
Yes, since a move is always available until the game ends and the game is guaranteed to terminate, a draw cannot occur.
inline_prompts: Fennec and Snuke are playing a board game. You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of positive integers of length N. Also, there is a set S, which is initially empty. Fennec and Snuke take turns performing the following operation in order, starting with Fennec. - Choose an index i such that 1\leq A_i, subtract 1 from A_i, and if i\notin S, add i to S. Note that a player may not choose an index with A_i = 0; only indices with A_i ≥ 1 are valid. - If S=, the game ends and the player who performed the last operation wins. Note that it can be proven that until a winner is determined and the game ends, players can always make a move (there exists some i such that 1\leq A_i). Both Fennec and Snuke play optimally to win. Determine who will win. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print Fennec if Fennec wins, or Snuke if Snuke wins. Constraints - 1\leq N\leq 2\times 10^5 - 1\leq A_i\leq 10^9 (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
